source.paper: What Teleportation Would Require: A Falsifiable Specification, condition C1, roadmap step 2
source.preregistration: Preregistration: The Empty-Middle Limit of Atom Transfer (Claude Doc, draft of 2026-11-25)

question: Can a physical guide between two traps act as the distance-independent mediator mode that C1 asks for, and if not, where does it stop working?

hypotheses.H1: For at least one of G1 to G3, every grid distance up to 1 mm is PASS at the generous budget.
hypotheses.H2: Without noise, T_req grows as d^2 for G1 and as d for G2 and G3.
hypotheses.H3: The paper's sentence that a chain cannot give an empty middle, tested with G3 without noise.

expectation_before_any_run: D* of a few micrometres at the reference budget and some tens of micrometres at the generous one, so MICROSCALE ONLY, with transfers about a hundred times slower than ordinary transport at the guide's own speed.

model.units: hbar = 1; energies in rad/s, times in s
model.middle_occupation: Population in every mediator mode, explicit or eliminated
model.integrator: Strang split: exact diagonal phases and an exact exponential of the coupling in span{A, B, rA, rB}; steps a multiple of 4000 with max |E| dt <= 0.5
model.far_modes: A mode is explicit when |E| <= 100 Omega max(1, r / 10), r its coupling relative to the resonant mode's (the larger of |rA| and |rB|); every other mode enters by adiabatic elimination: shift and exchange -sum (Omega_i r_i)(Omega_j r_j) / E on A and B, and population |sum Omega r c / E|^2 counted in P_mid; elimination holds only while the eliminated population stays at most elimination_cap times the trap population

noise.trap_offsets: dA, dB ~ Normal(0, 1/T2*) per seed, quasi-static
noise.lattice_disorder: on-site energies ~ Normal(0, sigma_W) per seed and site; traps tuned to the realized resonant mode first

designs.G0: Control: one mode at resonance, coupling independent of d
designs.G1: Free 1D hard-wall guide of length d + 1 um, lowest mode, couplings 0.5 um inside each end
designs.G2: The same guide, mode with energy nearest E_kin, couplings at that mode's antinode nearest each end
designs.G3: Lattice chain, spacing 0.532 um, smallest odd site count N with (N - 1) a >= d, A on the first site, B on the last, band-centre mode

search.loss_cap: a setting with exp(-Gamma T) < 0.90 is a loss-cap fail and is not run
search.mode_cap: a setting with more than 400 explicit modes is a mode-cap fail and is not run
search.elimination_cap: a setting whose eliminated population exceeds 0.1 of the trap population at any sample on any seed is an elimination-cap fail and its numbers are not kept; on that seed the middle then holds more than a tenth of the atom, so over eight dev seeds, or without noise, its M exceeds 0.01 and it cannot pass
search.selection: largest dev margin min[(F - 0.90)/0.10, (0.01 - M)/0.01], ties to shorter T; if none passes, the largest-margin setting goes forward

seeds.unit: seed: one draw of trap offsets and, for G3, lattice disorder; settings and time steps are never units
seeds.draws: numpy SeedSequence(seed).spawn(2): first child gives (zA, zB), second gives one standard normal per lattice site

heldout.rule: int(sha256(salt + ':' + str(i)).hexdigest()[:8], 16) for i in 0..count-1, generated only at the held-out run

noiseless.order: settings tried by increasing T; stop at the first with P_B(T) >= 0.90 and M < 0.01
noiseless.fit: least-squares slope of log T_req on log d over the 17 grid distances from 10 um to 1 mm

cell.PASS: lower bound of F >= 0.90 and upper bound of M < 0.01
cell.FAIL: upper bound of F < 0.90, or lower bound of M >= 0.01, or every setting hit the loss, mode or elimination cap, or the held-out run of the selected setting hit a cap

rules.limit: d* is the largest grid distance that is PASS with every shorter one; u is the shortest FAIL; D* is the largest d* across G1 to G3
rules.inputs: H2 and H3 use only noiseless records that carry this protocol's design hash; a design missing any of its 17 is INCOMPLETE for H2, and G3 missing any is INCOMPLETE for H3. The held-out run refuses, before any held-out seed exists or any file is written, unless all 225 cells, the G0 control and the 51 noiseless records are present and carry that hash

checks.V2: on the first dev seed, doubling the explicit window and its mode cap at each selected setting changes F and M by less than 1e-4, or by less than a tenth of the distance from the nearer bound of that cell's dev interval to the threshold
checks.V3: G0 at 1 kHz with its dev-selected pulse area is PASS at the reference budget
checks.V4: every selected setting re-run with the A side first is FAIL on M; a re-run past the elimination cap counts as FAIL on M, since the middle then holds more than a tenth of the atom on some seed
checks.V5: every result record carries the SHA-256 of this protocol's content without its status and registration date, and it matches
checks.V6: no held-out seed appears in any development log before the held-out run
checks.V7: at 1 um, at least one of G1 to G3 is PASS at the generous budget
checks.V8: on the first dev seed, doubling the step count at each selected setting changes F and M by less than 1e-4, or by less than a tenth of the distance from the nearer bound of that cell's dev interval to the threshold

amendments_before_freeze: Explicit modes are those within +-100 Omega max(1, r / 10) of resonance, r a mode's coupling relative to the resonant mode's, so every eliminated mode's coupling is under a tenth of its detuning; every other mode enters by adiabatic elimination. The draft's 'at least 8 per side' rule is dropped because it forced stiff explicit modes far outside the window. The scaling by r changes nothing below about 16 um; without it, G1 at 1 mm, whose traps sit where the lowest mode is small and so couple to higher modes up to 640 times harder, gave an eliminated middle occupation above 1.
The draft's solver tolerance (relative 1e-9, absolute 1e-11) is replaced by the fixed-grid Strang integrator above and check V8.
Settings with more than 400 explicit modes are mode-cap fails: they put several modes within the coupling of resonance, so the middle cannot stay near-empty.
G2's couplings sit L(1 - 1/n) apart, within 1 um of d; the grid distance d is still the one reported.

V2 and V8 also pass a change smaller than a tenth of the distance from the cell's nearer dev-interval bound to its threshold, since such a change cannot move a verdict. In development, G1 at 10 um (reference) selected a fast, failed transfer with F = 0.003 and M = 0.25, where doubling the steps or the window changed M by 1.3e-4 on the first dev seed; under the draft rule that alone would make H1 INVALID. V2 also doubles the mode cap with the window.

V5 hashes the protocol's content without status and registered, so a development search run before the freeze stays bound to the frozen protocol, and the held-out runner refuses any selected setting whose record carries another hash.

Elimination cap. The per-mode rule bounds each eliminated mode but not their sum, and in development G1 at 100 um (generous, 42.17 Hz, area 10) reported a middle occupation of 1.29 with its reduced state still normalized; on the first dev seed, doubling the window lowered it to 0.59. A setting whose eliminated population exceeds 0.1 of the trap population at any sample is now an elimination-cap fail. Such a setting cannot pass on dev seeds or without noise, so no verdict changes, and every kept run reports a middle occupation of at most 1. V4 counts a reversed re-run past the cap as FAIL on M.

Inputs are checked. H2 and H3 read only noiseless records made under this protocol and are INCOMPLETE, a new verdict for them, when any is missing, so a partial or stale search no longer reads as a finished one. The held-out run checks the whole development search before it makes a held-out seed or writes a file, so a missing or stale record cannot use up the held-out split.
